<h1>Martin Preiß</h1>

<div class="accent-line"></div>

<p class="intro">
I am a political scientist with a Master's degree in Political
Science from the University of Freiburg and an academic background
in political science and theology. My research interests lie at
the intersection of political science and data science, with a
particular focus on political behaviour and quantitative empirical
research. In my Master's thesis, I examined the determinants of
electoral participation by comparing classical statistical methods
with machine learning approaches using survey data from the
GESIS Panel.
</p>

<p class="intro">
I am interested in the application of computational methods to
social and political phenomena and the methodological challenges
associated with their integration into social science research.
My broader research interests include political communication,
the transformation of digital public spheres, the ethical and
political implications of artificial intelligence and the role
of emerging technologies in international relations. Through my
academic work and independent programming projects, I aim to
further develop my expertise in computational social science
and interdisciplinary research.
</p>

<div class="project-description">
<h3>Explaining Voter Turnout</h3>
<span class="project-meta">Master's Thesis · R · Machine Learning</span>
<p>Comparing logistic regression and machine learning

federal election using survey data from the GESIS Panel.</p>
